_doc: openHC's configuration of the EA3's ADAU1451. See README.md in this directory.
The DSP has no program of its own: it boots with its PLL off and its core
idle, and the host loads everything over I2C. init below is the part's
control-register setup (clocks, serial ports, routing), decoded from a
stock unit's registers; mkfw.py puts it in the firmware together with the
program when one is given (mkfw.py --program). The program is openHC's own,
built by SigmaStudio+ in CI and never committed.
The knobs and cells are the parameter side. Their addresses are those of
the program a stock unit runs, read off a running unit: that program reads
every knob as an INDEX 0..48 from a parameter cell and looks the setting up
in a 49-entry table. A program with another layout brings its own
addresses here. The table CONTENTS are computed by mkfw.py from the designs
below. Nothing here comes from a Control4 or Analog Devices file.
A cell's value (an integer) or words (8.24 numbers, or "0x..." raw) are
written at boot; a run value, if it has one, is what
audiod sets once it is up.
A knob with choices is a selector: the choice's words are written, the
first one at boot. Every other knob is 49 steps with 24 as its neutral,
because that is the size of
the program's tables: tone and EQ steps are step_db apart (0.5 dB gives
-12..+12 dB), balance steps are 100/24 percent (-100..+100).
Change a design here and rebuild; the web UI shows exactly these knobs.
Control registers (0xF000-0xF8FF, 16 bits each), written in this order
after a soft reset (every register but the PLL's back to its default) and
before the program. Only what differs from the default after that reset,
plus the PLL, which a soft reset keeps. Values are a stock EA3's, read off
the unit (2026-10-26); meanings are from the public ADAU1452/1451/1450
datasheet (Rev. C). The driver waits for PLL lock after PLL_ENABLE goes to
1: the control port answers nothing until it locks. count: that many
consecutive registers, all set to value.
Clocking: every serial port is a slave, and the core's frame rate is
serial input 0's (LRCLK_IN0). Serial input 3 alone runs on its own clocks
(BCLK_IN3/LRCLK_IN3) and reaches the core through ASRC 0: that is the
asynchronous stream, most likely the CE5300's I2S1. The clock generators
feed nothing here: no port is a master and nothing selects them.

writes.meaning: PLL_ENABLE: off, so the PLL settings below take effect when it is turned on
PLL_CTRL0: feedback divider x96
PLL_CTRL1: input prescaler /8, 24.576 MHz MCLK -> 3.072 MHz into the PLL
PLL_CLK_SRC: core and clock generators run on the PLL, 3.072 MHz x 96 = 294.912 MHz
MCLK_OUT: CLKOUT pin off (its rate field says 24.576 MHz, unused)
PLL_ENABLE: on; the driver waits for PLL_LOCK (0xf004) before the next write
POWER_ENABLE0: serial inputs 0-3, serial outputs 0-3, both ASRC banks and clock generators 1-3 on
ASRC_MUTE: ASRCs 1-7 muted, ASRC 0 open; LOCKMUTE ramps ASRC 0 down while it has no lock
CLK_GEN1_M: /8 (base 294.912 MHz/1024/8 = 36 kHz; unused)
CLK_GEN2_M: /8 (unused)
CLK_GEN3_M: /5 (unused)
CLK_GEN3_N: x1 (unused)
MP6_MODE: multipurpose output with pull-up, driven by the program (board use unknown)
MP7_MODE: multipurpose output with pull-up, driven by the program (board use unknown)
BCLK_OUT0..3_PIN: slow slew, lowest drive, pull-down off
LRCLK_OUT0..3_PIN: slow slew, lowest drive, pull-down off
SDATA_OUT0..2_PIN: slow slew, lowest drive, pull-down off
SDATA_OUT3_PIN: fastest slew, lowest drive, pull-down off (the one output pin set apart)
ASRC_INPUT0: ASRC 0 takes serial input channels 40/41, i.e. SDATA_IN3 left/right
ASRC_OUT_RATE0: ASRC 0 converts to SDATA_OUT0's frame rate, the outputs' clock
SOUT_SOURCE0..23: every serial output channel pair comes from the DSP core's outputs
SERIAL_BYTE_3_0: SDATA_IN3 slave to BCLK_IN3/LRCLK_IN3, I2S, 24-bit, 2 x 32-bit slots
SERIAL_BYTE_3_1: SDATA_IN3 at the base rate of clock generator 3 (only a master uses either)
SPDIF_RESTART: S/PDIF receiver resumes after relock (powered off: POWER_ENABLE1 is 0)
START_PULSE: the core runs one frame per serial input 0 frame (LRCLK_IN0)

knobs.label: Mode
knobs._design: the program's output selector, one-hot per channel (left 0x0db5..8, right 0x0db9..c), mapped off a stock unit. Tone shapes with bass and treble, EQ with the ten bands, Flat bypasses both, Test tone plays the program's oscillator. The first choice is the boot one

knobs.label: Loudness
knobs._design: the program's loudness selector, two-way per channel (left 0x0db1..2, right 0x0db3..4)

knobs.label: Bass
knobs._design: the HC-800's tone stage (alsa-ohceq): RBJ shelf, slope 1

knobs.label: Balance
knobs._design: linear, as alsa-ohceq: +100 silences the left channel. Which table is the left output is NOT yet confirmed by ear

cells._doc: 0..Max Volume through the program's volume curve. Written 0 at boot so nothing plays while the box comes up; audiod sets the run value once it has restored the output's saved level and tone. openHC sets each output's level in ALSA, as on the HC-800, so the DSP runs it full
the program's mute: these words are stock's 'on' (its Master switch writes 0, 0 for off). The program boots it half set, so it is written; silence at boot is Volume's job
which of the program's two volume curves Volume indexes
index into the program's -12..+12 dB gain table at 0x0060
the program's oscillator level, index into its -24..0 dB table at 0x002f; 8 is the program's own value
the program's version cell. No value: never written, and the ReadBack prefix makes the kernel read it fresh every time
